topicName: Regression Metrics: MSE, RMSE, MAE, R2, and MedianAbsoluteError
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Regression Metrics in Scikit-Learn"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When building machine learning models for regression tasks, evaluating their performance accurately is critical. Scikit-learn provides a comprehensive module, sklearn.metrics, which contains various utility functions to calculate error and accuracy scores for continuous target variables."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Regression Metrics Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mean Squared Error (MSE): Measures the average of the squares of the errors. It heavily penalizes large errors."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE): The square root of MSE, bringing the error metric back to the same units as the target variable."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mean Absolute Error (MAE): Measures the average magnitude of absolute errors, making it more robust to outliers than MSE."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"R-squared (R2) Score: Represents the proportion of variance in the dependent variable that is predictable from the independent variables."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Median Absolute Error: Computes the median of all absolute differences, offering extreme robustness to outliers."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementation in Python"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a complete implementation showing how to calculate these metrics using Scikit-learn."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error, r2_score, median_absolute_error

# True target values and model predictions
y_true = [3.0, -0.5, 2.0, 7.0]
y_pred = [2.5, 0.0, 2.0, 8.0]

# Calculating metrics
mse = mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred)
rmse = np.sqrt(mse)
mae = mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred)
r2 = r2_score(y_true, y_pred)
med_ae = median_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred)

print(f"MSE: {mse}")
print(f"RMSE: {rmse}")
print(f"MAE: {mae}")
print(f"R2 Score: {r2}")
print(f"Median Absolute Error: {med_ae}")"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Choosing the Right Metric"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Selecting the correct evaluation metric depends heavily on your dataset and business requirements. If your dataset contains significant outliers that should heavily impact the loss, use MSE or RMSE. If you want a metric that treats all errors equally and is easy to interpret in the original units, MAE or Median Absolute Error are preferable choices. R2 is ideal for understanding how well your model explains the variance of the data relative to a naive baseline."}]
